title: MCP (Model Context Protocol)
description: What MCP is, why it matters for the future of AI tools, and how it creates a universal standard for AI-tool connections.

data.text: The Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open standard created by Anthropic for connecting AI assistants to the systems where data and context live. Think of it as a universal adapter: instead of building custom integrations for every database, API, and file system, MCP defines a single protocol that any AI model can use to access any MCP-compatible tool.

Before MCP, every AI tool provider built custom integrations. If you wanted ChatGPT to access your PostgreSQL database, you built a custom plugin. If you wanted Claude to read your Google Drive, you built another custom integration. Each integration was one-off, brittle, and tied to a specific AI model. MCP replaces this fragmentation with a single, model-agnostic protocol.

data.text: MCP uses a client-server architecture. The MCP client lives inside the AI host (like Claude Desktop or Cursor). MCP servers are lightweight processes that expose tools, resources, and prompts over a standardized interface. Communication happens over JSON-RPC 2.0, typically via stdio for local tools or SSE for remote services.

data.title: Three core MCP primitives:
items: Tools — functions the AI can call (e.g., read_file, query_database, send_email)
Resources — data exposed to the AI (e.g., file contents, database schema, API responses)
Prompts — pre-built prompt templates the AI can use as starting points

data.text: An MCP server is a small program that implements the MCP protocol and exposes your tools. The most common way to build one is with the official MCP SDK, available for TypeScript, Python, and other languages. A minimal TypeScript MCP server is under 50 lines of code — it defines tool schemas, implements handlers, and registers them with the MCP runtime.

data.text: The MCP ecosystem is growing rapidly. Anthropic and community contributors have built servers for filesystems, PostgreSQL, Slack, GitHub, Google Drive, and many more. Tools like MCPHub and the Smithery registry help users discover and install MCP servers. The model-agnostic design means servers built today will work with future AI models.

data.title: MCP is the USB-C of AI integrations
data.text: Just as USB-C standardized device charging, MCP aims to standardize how AI systems connect to data and tools. A well-designed MCP server built today should work with any future MCP-compatible AI assistant — a durable investment.

data.title: Summary
points: MCP is an open standard for connecting AI models to external tools and data
It replaces custom integrations with a single, model-agnostic protocol
Three primitives: Tools (callable functions), Resources (exposed data), Prompts (templates)
MCP uses JSON-RPC over stdio (local) or SSE (remote)
The ecosystem includes servers for databases, files, APIs, and communication tools
MCP is model-agnostic — servers built today should work with future AI systems
data.takeaway: MCP's long-term impact may be less about any single feature and more about creating a durable, open interoperability layer for the AI tool ecosystem.
